contest: Most silver held when the round ends.

story.line: Silver gives rivals gifts that pay you back, and you choose who gets them.
story.greatGame: Round I you take Party Gifts and Toast, recruit Kingmakers, and hand out silver for followers. Round II you pick who wins the silver contest with Kingmakers at round end, and Sweet Nothings turns your silver into the colors for Ballroom Dancers. Round III you fill Silver spaces, cash Ballroom Dancers for about +12, and take Largesse for +10. Rivals take your gifts but watch who you are making king.
freshStart: Open House (round I space): Each rival +1 silver. +2 followers per rival in round I, +3 in round II, +4 in round III.
Thank-You Notes (round II space): +3 silver. +1 follower per rival holding silver.
Charity Auction (round III space): Give away as much of your silver as you want, split evenly among rivals; you keep what is left over. +2 followers per silver given.
Hosts (member): Round Start: each rival +1 silver. +2 followers.
Doting Aunts (member): On Use, once per round: give a rival 2 of your silver. +3 followers.

cards.name: Toast
cards.text: +3 silver in round I, +6 in round II, +9 in round III. Each rival +1 silver in round I, +2 in round II, +3 in round III.
cards.bestTurn: Round III, last turn before scoring: I take Toast for +9 silver, which tips me past the leader in the silver contest for +10 followers; each rival gets 3, but nobody can pass my pile.
cards.topCase: Round III, used once a round: +9 silver against Build Up's +5 green or Harvest's +5 of any colors. Rivals get 9 between them, so the edge over each is +6. About 1.5 times the best growing space; does not break the game.
cards.ideaWhy: A big pile for you and a small one for everyone: the color's gift in its plainest form.
cards.ties: Feeds every rival's silver count, so it can hand the silver contest to someone if you take it too early.
cards.coryNotes: Cory, Oct 31: "Silver round I keeps Toast". Nov 6 ("yes."): copying Toast gifts the rivals too.
cards.why: The color's dependable growing space; solid, not a moment anyone retells.
cards.short: Round III, last turn: +9 silver passes the leader, win the +10.

cards.name: Polish
cards.text: Turn 2 of your silver into 4 of any colors.
cards.bestTurn: Round I, holding the 3 silver from Toast: I turn 2 into 2 red and 2 blue and buy the member I could not afford.
cards.topCase: Round III, built around it: still 2 silver into 4, so +2 resources net, against +9 on Toast or +10 followers on Largesse. Flat; it never grows.
cards.ideaWhy: A currency swap with a small bonus; turning resources into other colors is Yellow's job, and Sweet Talk and Sweet Nothings already swap silver.
cards.ties: Needs silver from somewhere else first, and gives rivals nothing, so it is the one Silver space nobody else at the table feels.
cards.coryNotes: Cory, Nov 4: "yeah allow silver i guess" (may pick silver among the 4). Nov 5: "Polish animation is slow."
cards.why: The space players would miss least: +2 net, no gift, and the same swap as Sweet Talk and Yellow.
cards.short: Round I: turn 2 silver into 4 colors, buy a member early.
cards.risk: Swapping silver into colors is Yellow's job, like Makeover.

cards.name: Party Gifts
cards.text: Give rivals up to 3 silver from the bank, split as you choose. +2 followers per silver you give.
cards.bestTurn: Round I, first turn: I give 3 silver to the player with the least silver and take +6 followers; the player most likely to win the silver contest gets none.
cards.topCase: Round III: still +6 followers against Largesse's +10 or Toast's +9. Round I it is +6 against Harvest's +3, about twice, but rivals hold 3 more silver. Does not break the game.
cards.ideaWhy: Give rivals silver, get followers: the whole color on one space.
cards.ties: You pick who gets the silver, so it steers the silver contest a little every round.
cards.coryNotes: Cory, Oct 31: "No. 3 silver given out. 2 followers per silver" (his numbers).
cards.why: Strong round I turn and the color's clearest idea, but it is the same move as Largesse and Kingmakers at a smaller size.
cards.short: Round I: give 3 silver to the poorest rival, take +6 followers.

cards.name: Sweet Nothings
cards.text: +3 silver. Give rivals up to 3 of your silver, split as you choose: +2 of any colors each.
cards.bestTurn: Round II with 3 silver in hand: +3 silver, then give 3 away for +6 of the colors I need; I recruit a member costing 6 that I could not touch before.
cards.topCase: Round III: same +6 any for 3 silver handed out, net +6 resources and a level silver pile, against +9 on Toast. Fine; does not break the game.
cards.ideaWhy: Give your own silver away, get twice as much of other colors back.
cards.ties: Lowers your own silver and raises rivals', so it pulls against the silver contest; it swaps silver for colors at Polish's rate.
cards.why: His pick for the slot; a real gift with a real payback.
cards.short: Round II: give away 3 silver for 6 colors, recruit a 6-cost member.
cards.risk: Swapping silver into colors is Yellow's job, like Makeover.

cards.name: Sweet Talk
cards.text: +3 silver. Then turn as many of your silver as you want into other colors.
cards.bestTurn: Round II, holding 9 silver after Toast and gifts: +3, then turn all 12 into the exact red and blue for a 12-cost member and recruit it this turn.
cards.topCase: Round III: +3 silver plus turning a pile of 15 into whatever colors you need. The gain is the +3; the swap only lets the pile spend. Strong for a round II space, not broken.
cards.ideaWhy: Cash your silver into the colors you need.
cards.ties: Same shape as Yellow's Makeover ("+4 yellow, then rearrange your resources into any mix of colors.") one round earlier, and Cory's direction gives translating to Yellow.
cards.coryNotes: Cory, Oct 31: "Sweet Talk might be a little too strong, but thats ok. I like an R2 thats close to an R3".
cards.why: He likes it, but it overlaps Yellow's swap; the overlap is his call.
cards.short: Round II: turn 12 silver into colors for a 12-cost member.
cards.risk: Swapping silver into colors is Yellow's job, like Makeover.

cards.name: Largesse
cards.text: Give rivals 12 silver from the bank, split as you choose. +10 followers.
cards.bestTurn: Round III: I split the 12 as 6, 5 and 1 so the rival leading on followers gets 1 and the silver contest's +10 goes to someone far behind; I take +10.
cards.topCase: Round III, once: +10 followers against Initiation's free member costing 10 or less or Toast's +9; rivals gain 12 between them, about +4 each. In line with other round III spaces; does not break the game.
cards.ideaWhy: One big gift, one big payback, and you choose who wins the silver.
cards.ties: Decides the round III silver contest for a rival of your choice, the most direct kingmaking in the game.
cards.coryNotes: Cory, Nov 1: "a little bit of an issue, but I think it's interesting". Nov 5: "Largesse should have to give 12. And give 10 followers."
cards.why: His numbers; a real choice, though it hands the last silver contest to someone else.
cards.short: Round III: hand out 12 silver to crown a trailer, take +10.

cards.name: Godparent
cards.text: On Use, once per game: give one of your members to a rival. Gain followers equal to its cost.
cards.bestTurn: Round III: I used my 10-cost member's abilities, then give it to the player in last place and take +10 followers.
cards.topCase: Round III with a 10-cost member to give: +10 followers once, about one Largesse. The rival also gets the member's followers and ability. Fine; does not break the game.
cards.ideaWhy: Near twin of Guest of Honor in this color and of White's Farewell ("Cast out one of your members to the discard pile, gain followers equal to its cost.").
cards.ties: Gives a rival a whole member, which raises their member count and their followers.
cards.why: Two other cards already give away or cash out a member; this one adds nothing they lack.
cards.short: Round III: give a used 10-cost member away for +10 followers.
cards.risk: Twin of Guest of Honor and White's Farewell.

cards.name: Caterer
cards.bestTurn: Round II: Toast, Party Gifts and Sweet Nothings in one round each pay me +2 silver, and Kingmakers adds one more at round end: +8 silver.
cards.topCase: Round III, built around gifts: about 4 gifts a round, +8 silver a round, near 16 a game. Fine; does not break the game.
cards.ideaWhy: Word for word the Silver Cloak ("Whenever you gift silver, +2 silver."), on a member.
cards.ties: Pushes you to gift more, so rivals hold more silver.
cards.coryNotes: Cory, Nov 1: "seems like a lot. but willing to see what balance testing shows" (when it was the cloak). Nov 7, on the cloak: "Silver is crazy wtf.... Put silver to +2".
cards.why: It is the cloak again; a player holding both gets the same thing twice.
cards.short: Round II: four gifts in one round pay +8 silver.
cards.risk: Word for word the Silver Cloak.

cards.name: Guest of Honor
cards.text: On Use, once per round: give a rival one of your members. +4 followers.
cards.bestTurn: Round II: I give my used-up 3-cost member to a rival and take +4 followers; I lose 1 follower of member worth, so +3.
cards.topCase: Round III, every round from round I: 3 uses, +12 followers, minus 3 members worth about 3. Net about +9 over a game. Fine.
cards.ideaWhy: Pass a guest you are done with to a rival, collect followers.
cards.ties: Moves members between cults, which changes member counts for Blue's contest and followers for White's.
cards.coryNotes: Cory, Nov 4: "i like the concept of it. maybe on use once per round?"
cards.why: He likes the idea; small payoff each round.
cards.short: Round II: give away a spent 3-cost member for +4 followers.

cards.name: Toastmaster
cards.text: Whenever you take a Silver space, +1 follower.
cards.bestTurn: Round II: I take Toast and Sweet Talk and get +2 followers.
cards.topCase: Over a game spent on Silver spaces, about 6 Silver spaces: +6 followers for 5. Flat.
cards.ideaWhy: Plain bonus for using your color.
cards.ties: None: nobody else at the table notices it.
cards.why: No moment and no one feels it; the same job as High Society.
cards.short: Round II: take Toast and Sweet Talk for +2 followers.

cards.name: Debutantes
cards.text: On Use, once per game: double your silver. Each rival +2 silver.
cards.bestTurn: Round III before my last turn: I hold 14 silver, use it for +14, rivals get +2 each, and I win the silver contest's +10 by a mile.
cards.topCase: Round III holding 15: +15 silver and the silver contest, against Largesse's +10. About 1.5 times; does not break the game.
cards.ideaWhy: Save silver, then double it once.
cards.ties: Gives each rival 2 silver but almost always settles the silver contest for you.
cards.coryNotes: Cory, Nov 1: kept in Silver's deck; worth 1 more follower, price unchanged, "to try".
cards.why: A real once-a-game moment, but 11 is a lot to pay for it.
cards.short: Round III holding 14 silver: +14, win the silver +10 by a mile.

cards.name: Smooth Talkers
cards.text: Your silver pays for any color.
cards.bestTurn: Round III: my 12 silver pays for a blue and red member outright, without a swap space.
cards.topCase: Round III: no new resources at all, only freedom to spend silver, which Sweet Talk already gives for a space. Flat for 12.
cards.ideaWhy: Silver is money that spends as any color.
cards.ties: Translating currencies is Yellow's job by Cory's direction, and Sweet Talk and Polish do it in this color.
cards.coryNotes: Cory, Nov 1: kept, "Your silver pays for any color.", expensive.
cards.why: Costs 12 and gives nothing new; three other Silver cards already swap silver.
cards.short: Round III: 12 silver pays for a red and blue member outright.
cards.risk: Swapping silver into colors is Yellow's job, like Makeover.

cards.name: Debt Collectors
cards.text: On Use, once per round: each rival gives you 2 silver, if they have it.
cards.bestTurn: Round III: after Largesse spread 12 silver around, I take 2 from each rival: +6 silver for me, -2 for each, and the silver contest swings to me.
cards.topCase: Round III, every round from round II: +6 silver a round, about +12 a game, and an 8-point swing in the silver contest against the leader. Fine; does not break the game.
cards.ideaWhy: Gift silver out, collect it back.
cards.ties: Taking resources from rivals is Magenta's job (steals), so it overlaps another color.
cards.coryNotes: Cory, Nov 5: "yeah make it once per round. just make it a touch cheaper."
cards.why: He tuned it; good loop with gifting, but it overlaps Magenta's steals.
cards.short: Round III: take 2 from each rival, +6 silver, silver contest swings.
cards.risk: Taking from rivals is Magenta's job, like Help Yourself.

cards.name: High Society
cards.text: Whenever a rival takes a Silver space, +1 follower.
cards.bestTurn: Round II: two rivals take Toast and Sweet Talk; I get +2 followers on their turns.
cards.topCase: Over a game, rivals take about 6 Silver spaces: +6 followers for 9. Rivals can avoid Silver spaces. Flat.
cards.ideaWhy: Rivals using your color pay you.
cards.ties: A small sting: rivals think twice before taking Silver spaces.
cards.why: Rivals feel it a little; the payoff is thin.
cards.short: Round II: rivals take Toast and Sweet Talk, +2 followers for you.

cards.name: Ballroom Dancers
cards.text: On Use, once per game: +2 followers per minion on Silver spaces.
cards.bestTurn: Round III, last turn: every Silver space is full, 6 minions, mine and rivals': +12 followers at once.
cards.topCase: Round III with all 6 Silver spaces taken: +12, against Largesse's +10. Does not break the game; bots rate it worth more than its price.
cards.ideaWhy: Fill the dance floor, then cash it in.
cards.ties: Makes you want rivals on Silver spaces, so you gift them reasons to go there.
cards.coryNotes: Cory, Nov 5: "I love ballroom!". Nov 6: "yes on ballroom dancers" (price up).
cards.why: He loves it; one big turn that the whole table helps build.
cards.short: Round III, last turn: 6 minions on Silver spaces pay +12 followers.

cards.name: Kingmakers
cards.text: Round End: give a rival 3 silver from the bank. +3 followers.
cards.bestTurn: Round II end, before contests: the leader holds 7 silver and a rival holds 5; I hand the rival 3, they take the silver contest's +6, and I take +3.
cards.topCase: Recruited round I: +9 followers over the game for 6, and three silver contests nudged your way. Fine; does not break the game.
cards.ideaWhy: Decide who wins the silver contest, and get paid.
cards.ties: Round end abilities happen before contests, so it can change who wins the silver contest every round.
cards.coryNotes: Cory, Nov 5: "should probably be kingmakers", "yes to kingmaker and ballroom".
cards.why: Cheap, and it lands exactly when the contest is scored: the name is the moment.
cards.short: Round II end: hand a rival 3 silver to steal the +6.

cards.name: Patron Saints
cards.text: Game End: +1 follower per silver member, anyone’s.
cards.bestTurn: Game end: the table holds 9 silver member counts, so +9 followers.
cards.topCase: Round III, Silver popular at the table: about 8 to 10 followers. Fine; does not break the game.
cards.ideaWhy: The more silver members anywhere, the better for you.
cards.ties: Makes you want rivals to own silver members; Guest of Honor and Godparent give them yours.
cards.coryNotes: Cory, Nov 5: "yeah patron saints". Nov 6: "oh Patron Saints is supposed to be game end!!", "and keep cost at 7".
cards.why: His pick; steady, no single turn to retell.
cards.short: Game end: 9 silver members around the table pay +9 followers.

overlaps: Toastmaster "Whenever you take a Silver space, +1 follower." and High Society "Whenever a rival takes a Silver space, +1 follower."

Godparent "On Use, once per game: give one of your members to a rival. Gain followers equal to its cost." and Guest of Honor "On Use, once per round: give a rival one of your members. +4 followers."; Godparent also matches White's Farewell "Cast out one of your members to the discard pile, gain followers equal to its cost. +1 white."
Caterer "Whenever you gift silver, +2 silver." is the Silver Cloak "Whenever you gift silver, +2 silver." word for word.

Polish "Turn 2 of your silver into 4 of any colors.", Sweet Talk "+3 silver. Then turn as many of your silver as you want into other colors.", Sweet Nothings "+3 silver. Give rivals up to 3 of your silver, split as you choose: +2 of any colors each." and Smooth Talkers "Your silver pays for any color." all swap silver for other colors, the job Cory gave Yellow (Makeover "+4 yellow, then rearrange your resources into any mix of colors.").

Debt Collectors "On Use, once per round: each rival gives you 2 silver, if they have it." takes from rivals, Magenta's job (Help Yourself "Steal 3 resources in round I, 4 in round II, 5 in round III from one rival.").

Party Gifts "Give rivals up to 3 silver from the bank, split as you choose. +2 followers per silver you give.", Largesse "Give rivals 12 silver from the bank, split as you choose. +10 followers." and Kingmakers "Round End: give a rival 3 silver from the bank. +3 followers." are one move at three sizes; that is the color's core, not a flaw on its own.
notes: Silver's own idea, gift silver and get paid, runs through Party Gifts, Largesse, Kingmakers and Ballroom Dancers and holds up. The weak spots are the four cards that swap silver into other colors (Yellow's job) and three twins: Caterer and the cloak, Toastmaster and High Society, Godparent and Guest of Honor. Every gift raises a rival's silver, so the color decides the silver contest for others more than it wins it for itself; Debutantes and Debt Collectors are the only ways back. Round III pays well (Largesse +10, Ballroom Dancers about +12).
storyShort: Gift rivals silver for followers, and choose who your gifts crown.
